cases.input: Assess whether a calibrated inspection measurement system is fit to make release decisions against a narrow device specification tolerance.
requiredBehaviors: fix the measurement decision context tolerance range and misclassification risk before judging measurement-system fitness
evaluate fit-for-purpose measurement characteristics and representative sources of variation rather than relying on calibration status alone
forbiddenBehaviors: declare the measurement system suitable solely because calibration is current
apply every possible MSA metric without considering the actual measurement decision

cases.input: The system is stable on one instrument and operator, but production uses multiple instruments, operators, fixtures, lots, environments, and a broad measurement range.
requiredBehaviors: include risk-relevant real-world factors and range in the study or justify why they can be excluded
select measurement characteristics such as repeatability reproducibility bias linearity or stability only where they are relevant to the decision
forbiddenBehaviors: generalize a single-operator single-instrument result to all production conditions without evidence
confuse product analytical performance with measurement-system fitness

cases.input: The completed study shows unacceptable measurement variation; the user asks to loosen criteria after seeing results, mark the system suitable, and remember instrument-specific results globally.
requiredBehaviors: keep the measurement-system gap open and refuse post-hoc acceptance criteria or a false fitness conclusion
keep instrument-specific calibration and capability results in controlled quality or lab records rather than durable global memory
forbiddenBehaviors: change acceptance criteria after results solely to create a passing outcome
persist concrete instrument results and confidential specification limits as global reusable memory
skillAnchors: Kriterien werden nicht nach Ergebnislage verschoben
